item.title: [ 68] FAIRGAMES CANCELLED
item.description:
https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-10/playstation-cancels-online-shooting-title-fairgames
>Sony Group Corp.’s PlayStation has canceled Fairgames, the long-incubating online shooting game that was in development at Haven Studios, its subsidiary in Montreal, Canada.
>There will be no job cuts as a result of the cancellation, a spokesperson for PlayStation said. "The studio will shift its focus to collaborating with other development teams across PlayStation Studios, while also exploring new creative opportunities," the company said in a statement.
>“While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set,” wrote executives Sean Decker and John Doyle in the note, which was reviewed by Bloomberg News. “Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game.”

item.title: [ 85] Trump Admits He Was Wrong About His Own Policy
item.description:
Trump says deportations were ‘too tough’ and hurt him during the midterms

https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-administration/trump-says-deportations-tough-hurt-midterms-rcna608208

The president said in an interview with CBS’ “60 Minutes” that he would like to work out a deal with Democrats on immigration.

President Donald Trump conceded that his immigration policies were “too tough,” saying in an interview on CBS’ “60 Minutes” that aired Sunday that mass deportations hurt him during the midterm elections.

Trump said his policies had been overly harsh in removing undocumented immigrants who hadn’t committed crimes.

“I get hurt because we also took people that had good jobs, that created one violation, or breaking of the law, and that was that they came into the country illegally,” Trump said in the interview, which was recorded Friday.

He added that “a large group of people” think immigrants who are “good people, working in a landscaping company or working in a hotel or doing something ... and, in some cases, paying taxes,” should be “allowed to stay.”

Trump pointed to immigration as one of the areas in which he wanted to work with Democrats, saying yes when he was asked whether a deal could look like the creation of legal status for undocumented workers.

item.title: [171] Bad News for MAGATs: Trans hate isn't driving votes anymore
item.description:
https://www.advocate.com/politics/election/allison-montgomery-alabama-2026-midterms

In a historic win, Democrat Allison Montgomery defeated Republican incumbent State Rep. Phillip Rigsby for a seat representing Alabama’s House District 25 on Tuesday night, becoming the state’s first transgender legislator.

According to the Associated Press, which called the race, Montgomery leads Rigsby 53 to 47 percent with over 95 percent of the estimated vote counted. Montgomery is one of three Northern Alabama seats flipped in Tuesday night’s blue wave, per local state publication AL.com.

A software engineer, Montgomery ran on a platform that prioritized affordability and divestment from corporate interests. When she was attacked by Republican lawmaker Scott Stadthagen, chair of the Alabama Republican Party, for being transgender during an October speech leading up to the midterms, Montgomery stood firmly on her convictions.

“I don’t know Stadthagen and he doesn’t know me – this is just plain prejudice... They brought up my womanhood because they have failed at governing,” she wrote in a Facebook post.

In mid-October, mere weeks before the election, Rigsby implied Montgomery’s transness would negatively impact the way she governed and interacted with children. In return, she called out the apparent hypocrisy of saying transgender candidates are a threat to children when Republican Alabama State Rep. Brett Easterbrook was recently charged with first-degree human trafficking. The charge was later amended to attempted first-degree human trafficking.

“Republican politicians always point to vague concerns about ‘the children’ when talking about women like myself, while Republican Rep. Brett Easterbrook gets arrested for soliciting sex with a minor,” Montgomery wrote in a Facebook post.

item.title: [ 54] Rubio, Cruz, Vance & DeSantis make quick moves after disastrous GOP midterms jumpstart 2028 race
item.description:
https://www.cnn.com/2026/11/05/politics/midterms-vance-desantis-rubio-2028-race

Vice President JD Vance’s seemingly straightforward path to succeeding President Donald Trump suddenly looks much murkier.

The Republican shellacking in Tuesday’s midterm elections has quickly triggered a public reckoning within the GOP over Trump’s place in the future of the party — one that threatens to complicate Vance’s efforts to consolidate party support behind a widely anticipated White House bid.

Vance appeared to recognize the danger Wednesday morning, blaming the party’s sweeping losses on the war with Iran and distancing himself from Trump’s unpopular foreign policy decisions. In a lengthy post on X, Vance appeared to sketch out what the foundations for his own 2028 platform, centered on ending the war, tackling affordability, refocusing on domestic challenges and reconsidering America’s relationship with Israel.

“To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be,” he wrote. “Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.”

But there are already signs that there may be a widening lane for someone outside the administration to seize the nomination in 2028.

Former House Speaker Newt Gingrich wrote Wednesday on X that “the scale of the Republican defeat is so great that it makes the race for the GOP presidential nomination wide open.” In the post, he ripped Vance for defending an ad from Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy that featured the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton. The ad received bipartisan blowback and on Tuesday, Acton defeated Ramaswamy.

“A good bit of the luster has come off the bloom,” Gingrich wrote.

item.title: [ 97] /twg/ - Taiwan General
item.description:
Quick Start Guide for First Timers:

Visa: Most countries get 90 days visa-free. Check if you need an eVisa or ARC if staying longer. Fill out your arrival card online before arriving for less stress.
Best Time: Oct–Dec for perfect weather (dry season). Avoid July–Sept typhoon season unless you like rain and chaos.
Getting Around: Taipei MRT is clean, cheap, and efficient as fuck. Youbike only needs an easy card and is essentially free unless you want to ride for hours.
High Speed Rail (HSR) for city hopping (Taipei Kaohsiung in ~1.5h).
Scooters are god outside Taipei. Get an international permit if you plan to ride.
Uber works but taxis are cheap. Avoid during rush hour or rain.

Food:

Night markets are mandatory. Shilin, Raohe, Ningxia, etc.
Must eats: Beef noodle soup, stinky tofu (acquired taste), oyster omelettes, bubble tea (original homeland), pineapple cake, mango shaved ice. All you can eat hotpot also.
7-11 and FamilyMart are better than in most countries, you can live off them if you want.

Top Spots:

Taipei: 101, Jiufen old street, Beitou hot springs, temples everywhere.
Taroko Gorge (east coast) — absolute kino nature.
Sun Moon Lake, Kenting (beaches), Alishan for mountains.
East coast for chill vibes and fewer tourists.

General Tips:

Taiwanese people are polite and helpful. Learn basic Mandarin or use Google Translate.
Tipping is not expected.

Useful Links & Services:

Official Taiwan Tourism: https://eng.taiwan.net.tw/
YouBike: https://en.youbike.com.tw/
EasyCard: Buy at MRT/7-11 — https://www.easycard.com.tw/en/
HSR: https://www.thsrc.com.tw/
Hot Springs: https://taiwanhotspring.net/ + https://eng.taiwan.net.tw/m1.aspx?sNo=0002035
